events.content: Add view transitions to this product gallery app. When navigating from the grid to a product detail page, the product image should smoothly morph between the thumbnail and the large detail image using a shared element transition. Page navigations should slide directionally. Suspense loading states should transition smoothly from skeleton to content. All animations must respect the user's prefers-reduced-motion preference.

content.text: Add view transitions to this product gallery app. When navigating from the grid to a product detail page, the product image should smoothly morph between the thumbnail and the large detail image using a shared element transition. Page navigations should slide directionally. Suspense loading states should transition smoothly from skeleton to content. All animations must respect the user's prefers-reduced-motion preference.

events.content: I'll explore the product gallery app structure and Next.js docs for view transitions, then implement shared image morphing, directional slides, and reduced-motion-aware skeleton transitions.

matches.content: React's `<ViewTransition>` component integrates with the browser's [View Transitions API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/View_Transition_API) to handle this declaratively. You name the elements that should persist, and the browser animates between their old and new positions.

View transitions work in the App Router with no configuration. The App Router uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries), which contain all stable React 19 changes as well as newer features like `ViewTransition`. You do not need to install `react@canary` yourself.

`<ViewTransition>` animations are activated by [Transitions](https://react.dev/reference/react/useTransition), [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense), and [`useDeferredValue`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useDeferredValue). Regular `setState` calls do not trigger them. In Next.js, route navigations are transitions, so `<ViewTransition>` animations activate automatically during navigation.
Wrap both the grid thumbnail and the detail hero in `<ViewTransition>` with the same `name`:

Add the same props to both Step 1 snippets (`photo-grid.tsx` and `photo-content.tsx`). `default="none"` keeps each named image from running its own crossfade on every unrelated transition. Without it, every named `<ViewTransition>` animates whenever any transition runs on the page. When you add `default="none"` to a named pair, keep the explicit `share`. With `default="none"` and no `share` prop, the pair silently stops morphing.
Wrap the Suspense fallback in a `ViewTransition` with an exit animation, and the content in a `ViewTransition` with an enter animation:
As in Step 1, `default="none"` prevents this `ViewTransition` from animating during unrelated transitions, like the shared element morph.
Then wrap page content in a `ViewTransition` that maps transition types to directional animations:

events.content:
View transitions are wired up across the gallery using React’s `<ViewTransition>` component and the patterns from the Next.js view transitions guide.

### Shared element morph (grid → detail)
Product thumbnails and hero images share a `ViewTransition` name (`product-${slug}`) with `share="morph"` so the colored image block morphs from the grid cell to the detail layout.

### Directional page slides
- Forward navigation (`ProductGrid` links): `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}` — content slides left
- Back navigation (detail “Back to products” link): `transitionTypes={['nav-back']}` — content slides right
- Both pages wrap their content in matching `ViewTransition` enter/exit mappings
- The home page “Products” heading is anchored with `viewTransitionName: 'page-heading'` so it stays fixed during slides

### Suspense reveal transitions
Skeleton fallbacks use `exit="slide-down"` and loaded content uses `enter="slide-up"` on:
- Home page grid loading
- Product detail info loading (100ms async delay)

### Reduced motion
A `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` media query disables all view transition animations and skeleton pulse animations.

### Dependency note
`react` and `react-dom` were upgraded to canary (`19.3.0-canary`) because `ViewTransition` is not exported from stable React 19.1.0. This matches what Next.js 16’s App Router expects for this feature.

Run `npm run dev` and click between the grid and product pages to see the morph + directional slide animations. Refresh a product detail page to see the skeleton-to-content reveal.
